implementation_notes: The .NET realization is the immutable collections package: ImmutableList<T>, ImmutableDictionary<TKey,TValue>, ImmutableSortedSet<T> and the struct ImmutableArray<T> never change in place - each update returns a new instance, and ImmutableInterlocked supplies the interlocked exchange and update helpers for publishing such a value to other threads. The classic refcounted handle is not needed on a tracing GC: records with with expressions, IReadOnlyList<T> views and ImmutableArray<T>.Builder supply the value-style API, so a hand-rolled detach-on-write wrapper is justified only for large mutable buffers (pooled with ArrayPool<T>) where snapshotting a whole graph would be wasteful.
pitfalls: ImmutableArray<T> is a struct over a shared array: default(ImmutableArray<T>) is uninitialized and throws when used - check IsDefault, or start from ImmutableArray<T>.Empty.
A mutable element inside an immutable collection reintroduces aliasing; the collection is only as immutable as what it holds.
Converting to a Builder for a single change allocates; use Add/Remove/SetItem directly and batch through a Builder only for many changes in a row.
Immutable collections are not free under write-heavy load: each update copies a path, so a hot mutation loop belongs in a Builder or a plain mutable structure.
